newsitem.title: CROATIA: GraWE's Croatian unit sees rise in '97 income.
newsitem.headline: GraWE's Croatian unit sees rise in '97 income.

text.p: Croatian insurer Prima osiguranje d.d., 98 percent owned by Austria's Grazer Wechselseitige Versicherung AG (GraWE), expects premium income in 1997 to rise to over 100 million kuna, from 71.4 million last year.
Vjesnik daily said on Monday life insurance accounted for 82 percent in Prima's premium structure, while property and accident insurance accounted for 3.7 and 14.24 percent.
In 1995, Prima's premium income was 52.4 million kuna and its share in the Croatian insurance market was put at 1.86 percent, the paper said.
The country has 20 insurance companies. The biggest insurer is Croatia Osiguranje which had a 77.10 percent market share in 1995.

GraWE, Austria's sixth biggest insurer with annual premium income of 3.8 billion schillings, acquired a 98 percent stake in Prima osiguranje in 1990 as a first Western insurance company in Croatia. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
